references.text: Aaron and Hur are mentioned together earlier when they supported Moses' hands during the battle against Amalek. This shows their role as trusted leaders in Israel.
The elders of Israel are mentioned as those who went up the mountain with Moses, Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu. Here they receive instructions to wait.
While Moses was away, the people came to Aaron with their concerns, and he led them to make the golden calf. This shows the consequence of Moses' absence.
Moses appointed leaders to judge cases among the people. The expression 'the one who has a case' (בַּעַל דְּבָרִים) refers to the same type of legal function.
Moses reminds how he appointed judges to handle the people's matters and disputes, similar to the arrangement with Aaron and Hur.
Abraham said to his servants 'stay here' (שְׁבוּ־לָכֶם) while he and Isaac went further. The same linguistic construction and situation of waiting.
Contrast between Aaron's role as a stable leader in Exodus 24 and his failure to lead the people away from idolatry in Exodus 32.
Direct narrative connection: Verse 6 invites the seventy elders, while verse 14 explains that they remain below while Moses goes further up.
Preliminary instruction establishing the hierarchical separation between the people/elders and the leaders that unfolds in chapter 24.
Narrative contrast: Moses' call to wait (Ex 24) versus the people's immediate demand for gods when he did not return (Acts 7).
